paragraphs.context: As she spoke, Amy returned her contribution, with a nod and a smile
paragraphs.mainIdea: Amy gives May's things back with a friendly smile and leaves quickly, so that no one can thank her.
paragraphs.simple: As she spoke, Amy gave back May's things, with a nod and a smile. Then she hurried away, feeling it was easier to do a friendly act than to stay and be thanked for it.

paragraphs.context: “I’m afraid it is partly your own fault, dear. When Aunt spoke to me the other day
paragraphs.mainIdea: Mrs. March tells Jo that Aunt Carrol chose Amy because of Jo's own words, which Aunt quotes in her letter.
paragraphs.simple: Mrs. March says it is partly Jo's fault. When Aunt spoke to her some days before, she was sorry about Jo's blunt manners and too independent spirit. Now she writes as if she is repeating something Jo said. She says she planned first to ask Jo, but since 'favors burden her' and she 'hates French', she will not invite her. Amy is easier to teach, will be a good friend for Flo, and will be thankful for any help the trip gives her.

sentences.context: Because they are mean is no reason why I should be.
sentences.simple: The fact that they are unkind is no reason for me to be unkind.
sentences.grammar: The whole clause 'Because they are mean' is the subject of the sentence. 'Be' stands for 'be mean'. It is a little unusual to start a sentence this way.

sentences.context: feeling that virtue was not always its own reward
sentences.simple: She felt that being good did not always bring its own prize.
sentences.grammar: 'Virtue is its own reward' is a well-known saying. Here the writer says 'not always' to make a gentle joke about it.

sentences.context: I only did as I’d be done by.
sentences.simple: I only did to others what I would want them to do to me.
sentences.grammar: 'As I'd be done by' means 'as I would wish to be treated'. It is a short form of the Golden Rule, with 'done by' in the passive.
